trip.title: Utah Canyon Country
trip.subtitle: From the Rockies into the Red Rock West

days.title: Fort Collins → Black Canyon → Ouray, CO

options.name: Box Canyon Lodge & Hot Springs
options.note: Four spring-fed redwood soaking tubs terraced up the hillside behind the lodge, included with the room — the easiest way to get the soak without spending a time slot on it

options.name: Twin Peaks Lodge & Hot Springs
options.note: On-site hot spring pools and tubs, larger rooms, at the south end of Main Street

options.name: Beaumont Hotel
options.note: Restored 1886 landmark on Main Street — the grandest room in town, adults-oriented

items.title: Depart Fort Collins
items.detail: Load the car the night before. Long day, but it ends with a national park in it rather than just mileage.

items.title: Drive to Fairplay
items.detail: I-25 south, around Denver on C-470, then US-285 climbs over Kenosha Pass (10,001 ft) and drops into South Park — a treeless basin the size of a county, ringed by fourteeners.

items.title: Fairplay — first real break
items.detail: A 19th-century mining town at 9,950 ft. Gas, coffee and a proper stretch before the next stretch of mountains.

items.title: Drive to Gunnison over Monarch Pass
items.detail: US-285 over Trout Creek Pass, down the Arkansas headwaters past Salida, then US-50 climbs the Continental Divide at Monarch Pass (11,312 ft). Ears pop twice.

items.title: Lunch in Gunnison
items.detail: A college town on the Gunnison River and the last substantial place to eat before the canyon. Fuel up here too.

items.title: Drive to Black Canyon — South Rim
items.detail: US-50 west through the Curecanti reservoirs, then CO-347 climbs six miles to the rim. The park entrance is directly on the way to Ouray, not a detour.

items.title: Black Canyon of the Gunnison — South Rim
items.detail: A gorge so narrow and so deep that parts of the floor get half an hour of sunlight a day — 2,000 ft straight down to the river, and in places only 40 ft wide at the bottom. Drive the South Rim Road and stop at Gunnison Point, Chasm View, Painted Wall (the tallest cliff in Colorado at 2,250 ft) and Sunset View. All are short paved walks from the car park, which is what makes it work with a three-year-old and a newborn.
items.flag: The South Rim Road stays open until the first significant snowfall — usually mid-November, but it is weather-dependent, not a fixed date. The visitor center runs 9:00 AM–4:00 PM from Oct 1 with a lunch closure at 12:00–12:30. Check nps.gov/blca before you commit to the stop.

items.title: Drive to Ouray
items.detail: Back to US-50, west past Montrose, then US-550 south up the Uncompahgre valley. The San Juans fill the windscreen for the last twenty minutes.

items.title: Arrive Ouray — check in
items.detail: A Victorian mining town of a thousand people wedged into a box canyon, walled in on three sides. Everything is within four blocks.

items.title: Dinner in Ouray
items.detail: Main Street is two blocks long and has more good restaurants than a town this size has any business having. Walk from the hotel.

tips: Leave by 6:30 — arriving in daylight matters, and the Black Canyon overlooks are the point of the day.
Black Canyon entry is covered by the America the Beautiful and Senior passes.
Two Continental Divide crossings today, Kenosha and Monarch. Check cotrip.org the morning you go.
Ouray sleeps at 7,792 ft. Expect a cold night and a slow first hour for anyone who feels altitude.
Several Ouray hotels have their own hot-spring soaking tubs — worth choosing one for tonight, since it costs no time at all.
Pack the cooler the night before; South Park and the Gunnison stretch are thin on services.

momNotes.text: Question mark next to the Strater Hotel — wants to talk it through before booking.

stops.name: Black Canyon of the Gunnison — South Rim

days.title: Ouray → Million Dollar Highway → Telluride → Cortez

options.name: Holiday Inn Express Mesa Verde-Cortez
options.note: Ten minutes from the park entrance, indoor pool, full hot breakfast — the easy default with small children

options.name: Hampton Inn Mesa Verde
options.note: Same distance from the gate, free hot breakfast, reliable rooms

options.name: Retro Inn at Mesa Verde
options.note: Small independent motel, mid-century styling, cheaper than the chains

items.title: Drive the Million Dollar Highway south
items.detail: US-550 out of Ouray on a shelf blasted into the wall of the Uncompahgre Gorge — no guardrail, a sheer drop off the passenger side, and Bear Creek Falls dropping under the road at mile 2. This is the famous stretch.
items.flag: Red Mountain Pass is maintained all winter but can close on short notice in an early storm, and it is a serious road in bad weather. Check cotrip.org before you set off. If it is closed you lose nothing else — turn around and head straight for Telluride.

items.title: Red Mountain Pass and the Ironton overlooks
items.detail: Turn around at the pass (11,018 ft). The Red Mountain mining district on the way up is rust-orange rock with wooden headframes still standing in the trees, and the Ironton ghost town sits just below the summit. Drive it out and back — the pass is where the good part ends, and Silverton beyond it is another 45 minutes each way.

items.title: Drive back down to Ouray
items.detail: The same shelf road northbound, which is the better direction for the gorge views — the drop is now on the driver’s side and the town appears below you.

items.title: Box Cañon Falls, Ouray
items.detail: A 285-foot waterfall roaring inside a limestone slot barely wider than your shoulders, reached by a short steel walkway bolted to the canyon wall. Five minutes from the hotel, about ten minutes of walking, and genuinely thrilling for a three-year-old. Roughly $8 adult, $7 senior, $6 for ages 4–17.

items.title: Drive to Telluride
items.detail: North to Ridgway, then west and south up the San Miguel valley. Gentle going — no cliff edges — and the aspens should still be turning.

items.title: Lunch in Telluride
items.detail: The main street runs straight at a wall of mountains with Bridal Veil Falls at the end of it. Plenty of choice, and you are parked for the afternoon.

items.title: Telluride and the free gondola
items.detail: A free gondola climbs 1,750 ft over the ridge from Telluride to Mountain Village and back, running 6:30 AM to midnight through Oct 25. Fifteen minutes each way, cabins every few seconds, and a stroller rolls straight on. The view down into the box canyon at the top is the best thing you will see all day that costs nothing.

items.title: Drive to Cortez
items.detail: South on CO-145 over Lizard Head Pass (10,222 ft), past the Wilson peaks, then down through Rico and Dolores into the Montezuma Valley.

items.title: Arrive Cortez — check in
items.detail: Ten minutes from the Mesa Verde entrance, which is the whole point of sleeping here. An easy evening after a short driving day.

items.title: Dinner in Cortez
items.detail: A working town rather than a resort one, with honest food and no queues. Early night — tomorrow starts at 7:45.

tips: The lightest driving day between here and Utah: 152 miles, three and a half hours, and most of it before lunch.
Two passes above 10,000 ft. Check cotrip.org before Red Mountain in the morning and again before Lizard Head in the afternoon.

Ouray Hot Springs Pool is right in town if you would rather swap it for Box Cañon Falls — but it does not open until 11:00, and the waterslide and shallow activity pool are closed after Labor Day, so in October it is a soak rather than somewhere a three-year-old can play.
This is the day to buy anything you need for the desert. Cortez is the last real supermarket before Monument Valley.
Drive times today are padded above what routing engines report — US-550 and CO-145 are twisty mountain highways and the machines are optimistic about them.

days.title: Cortez → Mesa Verde → Monument Valley

options.name: Goulding's Lodge
options.note: Legendary lodge just west of the park, at the base of a mesa — John Ford's base for the Westerns. Rooms face east across the valley, there is a pool, a restaurant and a small museum, and it is the only full-service lodging in the area. Two miles outside the Tribal Park boundary, which matters for the gate hours below

items.title: Depart Cortez
items.detail: Breakfast at the hotel. The park gate is ten minutes away, which buys you an extra half hour on the mesa.

items.title: Drive to Mesa Verde — Chapin Mesa
items.detail: US-160 east to the gate, then the park road climbs 20 miles up onto the mesa. That climb is most of this hour — do not plan around the entrance sign.

items.title: Mesa Verde National Park — Chapin Mesa
items.detail: Start at the museum, then the Mesa Top Loop, then the Cliff Palace overlook. Ranger-led cliff dwelling tours are ticketed and sell out — book ahead or view from the rim, which is still remarkable.

items.title: Drive down off the mesa to Cortez
items.detail: The 20-mile park road again in reverse, then ten minutes west.

items.title: Lunch in Cortez
items.detail: Back where you started the day. Fuel up too — services thin out badly once you turn south.

items.title: Drive to Goosenecks
items.detail: US-160 west then US-163 south, crossing into Utah. Long, empty, beautiful. Skipping Goosenecks makes this a straight run to Monument Valley: 125 mi, 2 hr 15 min.

items.title: Goosenecks State Park
items.detail: A thousand-foot overlook onto the San Juan River folded back on itself five times. Twenty minutes at the rail is enough, and there are no guardrails to speak of — hold onto the three-year-old.

items.title: Drive to the Monument Valley overlook
items.detail: UT-261 south to US-163. The Mittens come into view about ten minutes out and it is worth the whole drive.

items.title: Wildcat Trail and the Mittens overlook
items.detail: Park at the tribal park visitor center. The full Wildcat loop is 3.2 miles and too much this late, but the overlook and the first stretch of trail give you the classic view without committing to it. Tribal park gates close at 5:00 PM from October 1 — be through by then.

items.title: Drive to Goulding's Lodge
items.detail: Back out to US-163 and a couple of miles west, just inside Utah.

items.title: Check in at Goulding's Lodge
items.detail: Rooms face the valley. Get the bags in and hands washed — dinner is early on purpose.

items.title: Dinner at the Stagecoach Dining Room
items.detail: The lodge restaurant, on site — no driving. Eating at 5:30 is deliberate: it puts dinner safely before sunset so nobody is negotiating with a hungry three-year-old during the best light of the day.

items.title: Sunset from the Goulding's terrace
items.detail: Sunset is 6:45 PM. You do not go anywhere for this — the terrace outside the dining room looks straight east across the valley at the Mittens, and the rock goes orange to red to purple over about half an hour.

items.title: Stargazing from the Goulding's grounds
items.detail: Step out from your room onto the lodge grounds. The moon is only about 8% lit on Oct 14, so the Milky Way should be plainly visible — this is among the darkest skies on the whole trip.

tips: The Tribal Park runs winter hours from Oct 1: gates open 8:00 AM, close 5:00 PM, last Scenic Drive entry 2:30 PM. Sunset and sunrise both fall outside that window.

The visitor center overlook is inside the gate but is not the Scenic Drive — the 2:30 PM last-entry rule applies to the 17-mile loop, not to walking out to the rim. Just be through the gate before 5:00 PM.
Mesa Verde's Wetherill Mesa road usually closes by mid-October, but Chapin Mesa — the part you want — stays open.
Book the Cliff Palace tour at recreation.gov ($5/person). It fills fast even in October.
Park entry at Mesa Verde is covered by America the Beautiful / Senior Pass. Monument Valley is a Navajo Tribal Park at $20/vehicle and is NOT covered.

momNotes.text: Circled "Senior Pass" against the Mesa Verde section — she has one, so park entry is covered. She circled it again on Days 5, 9, 11 and the packing list.
Star next to The View Hotel — her pick for Monument Valley. It has no availability for Oct 14, so the booking is Goulding's.
Question mark next to the guided Jeep tours. Decided against on cost — the Wildcat Trail covers the valley on foot for the price of the entry fee.

days.title: Monument Valley → Zion National Park

options.name: Cable Mountain Lodge
options.note: Suites on the Virgin River, canyon-wall views; walk to everything in Springdale

options.name: Desert Pearl Inn
options.note: Pool, river views, excellent for families; very limited rooms

options.name: Cliffrose Springdale
options.note: Lush gardens along the Virgin River, lovely setting

items.title: Drive to Forrest Gump Point
items.detail: US-163 north. Fifteen miles, and worth the early alarm.

items.title: Sunrise from US-163 — Forrest Gump Point
items.detail: Sunrise is 7:27 AM. This is the mile-marker-13 pullout where the highway runs dead straight at the buttes — the view everybody recognises. It is a public highway shoulder, so no gate and no fee, which matters because the tribal park does not open until 8:00 AM in October.

items.title: Drive back to Goulding's
items.detail: Same fifteen miles in reverse.

items.title: Breakfast at Goulding's and load the car
items.detail: Eat properly here. Today is the longest transit of the trip and the services between here and Kanab are thin.

items.title: Wildcat Trail full loop
items.detail: The complete 3.2-mile loop around West Mitten Butte, on the valley floor. Genuinely great, and genuinely a two-hour commitment that pushes everything below back by two hours and puts you in Springdale after dark. Only if you skipped it yesterday and are willing to trade the Zion evening.

items.title: Drive Monument Valley to Kanab
items.detail: US-163 south, US-160 west, US-89 north. Big, empty, and long — three and a half hours with one gas stop. The optional detours below hang off this leg.
items.flag: Page, AZ does not observe daylight saving but the Navajo Nation does. Crossing from Monument Valley into Page you gain an hour; crossing back into Utah you lose it again. Phones change on their own — trust the clock, not your sense of elapsed time.

items.title: Horseshoe Bend, Page AZ
items.detail: A 1.5-mile round-trip walk on sand to the overlook where the Colorado wraps 270 degrees around a sandstone fin. Add about 1 hr 15 min to the day including the walk and the parking fee. Note the clock: it is 10:20 AM trip time but 9:20 AM local, because Page stays on standard time.

items.title: Toadstool Hoodoos
items.detail: A flat 1.5-mile round trip off US-89 to a field of balanced boulders perched on soft pedestals. No fee, no gate, and the best kid-to-effort ratio on the trip. Adds about an hour, and only works if you have already given up on an early Zion arrival.

items.title: Lunch in Kanab
items.detail: The one proper meal stop between Monument Valley and Zion, and the last real town before Springdale. Excellent restaurants for its size, and everyone needs out of the car by now. Fuel up here too.

items.title: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary, Kanab
items.detail: The largest no-kill animal sanctuary in the country, in a red-rock canyon just north of town. Tours are free but must be booked ahead. Adds about 1 hr 30 min including the drive out and back.

items.title: Drive to Springdale
items.detail: US-89 north then UT-9 west through Mt Carmel Junction. The last twenty minutes drop into the canyon and it is a genuinely startling arrival.

items.title: Arrive Springdale — check in
items.detail: Early on purpose. Two nights here, so unpack properly.

items.title: Pa'rus Trail
items.detail: A 1.7-mile paved, flat trail along the Virgin River from the visitor center — the only trail in Zion open to strollers and bicycles. A gentle first look at the canyon walls without committing to a hike.

items.title: Dinner in Springdale
items.detail: The whole town is one street and it is all within walking distance of the hotels. Sunset is 6:53 tonight.

tips: Day 4 is 4 hrs 20 min of driving after a sunrise start. Pick ONE of the three optional stops below, not all three — most likely Toadstool (free, no detour) or Horseshoe Bend (iconic, 15 min off route).
The Navajo Nation observes daylight saving even though the rest of Arizona does not; your phone should match Utah time all day.

momNotes.text: Star and a smiley face next to the Pa'rus Trail — clearly a highlight for her.
Ranked Springdale lodging: Cable Mountain Lodge 1st, Desert Pearl Inn 2nd.

days.title: Zion National Park — Full Day

items.title: Drive to the Canyon Overlook trailhead
items.detail: UT-9 east through the Zion–Mount Carmel tunnel. Private cars are fine on this road all day — it is the Scenic Drive that is closed to cars, not this.

items.title: Canyon Overlook Trail (1 mi RT, moderate)
items.detail: Do this first, in your own car. The trailhead is at the east end of the tunnel. A short hike to a magnificent panorama over lower Zion Canyon. Some exposure on one side but well maintained; the three-year-old can walk most of it with help on a few rocky steps. Parking is very limited, which is the real reason to be here at 8:00.

items.title: Drive back to the Visitor Center
items.detail: Back down through the tunnel.

items.title: Park at the Visitor Center and pick up the shuttle
items.detail: The shuttle is running on Oct 16 (the Sept 13 – Oct 24 schedule, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, every 5–10 minutes), which means private vehicles are not allowed up the Scenic Drive. Strollers must be folded on board.

items.title: Shuttle to Zion Lodge — stop 5
items.detail: Roughly halfway up the canyon. The narration is genuinely good.

items.title: Lower Emerald Pools
items.detail: 1.2 miles, paved and flat: a wide trail to a pool beneath a dripping overhang that showers mist on everyone below. She will want to stand under it forever. This is the reliable option and the one to build the day around.

items.title: Lunch at the Zion Lodge café
items.detail: The lodge is right at shuttle stop 5, with a lawn and shade trees. The only food inside the canyon — everywhere else means riding back out.

items.title: Shuttle to Weeping Rock — stop 7
items.detail: Two stops up the canyon.

items.title: Weeping Rock — check status first
items.detail: 0.4 miles, very easy: a spring seeps through the canyon wall into a hanging garden of ferns with a gentle waterfall. The catch is that the Weeping Rock area was hit by a large rockfall in 2019 and the trails above it remain on long-term closure; the short trail itself has reopened and closed repeatedly since. Check the morning of — if it is closed, ride on to the Temple of Sinawava and walk the Riverside Walk instead.

items.title: Shuttle to the Temple of Sinawava — last stop
items.detail: The end of the line, past Big Bend and the Court of the Patriarchs.

items.title: Riverside Walk and the Temple of Sinawava
items.detail: The version of the Scenic Drive you actually get in October, all narrated, with no parking to fight over. The Riverside Walk at the end is 2.2 miles paved and stroller-friendly if there is energy left.

items.title: Shuttle back down to the Visitor Center
items.detail: The full run back down the canyon. Allow the full 40 minutes — it stops everywhere.

items.title: Back in Springdale
items.detail: Collect the car and walk into town.

items.title: Dinner in Springdale
items.detail: Second night, so try the other end of the street.

tips: The shuttle runs on your dates, so private cars cannot drive the Zion Canyon Scenic Drive. Park at the Visitor Center and ride.
No ticket or reservation is needed for the shuttle; just queue at the Visitor Center.
Strollers must be folded to board — a carrier is easier for the newborn.
The Narrows involves wading in cold water — skip it for this group.
Park entry by America the Beautiful / Senior Pass.
Last shuttle leaves the Visitor Center at 6:00 PM; last one down from the Temple of Sinawava is later, but do not cut it fine.

momNotes.text: Circled "Senior Pass" again in the Zion notes.
Her circled "Senior Pass" still applies — entry is covered, and the shuttle is free on top of that.

stops.name: Zion Visitor Center — shuttle all day

days.routeNote: Only the first two legs are driven. Everything inside the canyon is the park shuttle; private cars are not allowed up the Scenic Drive in October.

days.title: Zion → Kolob Canyons → Snow Canyon → Ivins

options.name: Black Desert Resort
options.note: Booked with the Chase travel credit. A new luxury resort in Ivins built into black lava flows, five minutes from Snow Canyon — closer to the park than downtown St. George is. Spa, pools, golf, several restaurants on site, and multi-bedroom units. Two nights here is the one genuinely restful stretch of the trip

options.name: Inn on the Cliff
options.note: Dramatic cliff-edge location, sweeping red-rock valley views, serene

options.name: Hilton Garden Inn St. George
options.note: Modern, pool, family-friendly. Sits off I-15 by the convention center, about 20 minutes from Snow Canyon

options.name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott
options.note: Spacious suites with kitchenette, excellent value, quiet — actually in Washington, UT, about 10 min east of St. George

options.name: The Inn at Entrada
options.note: Casitas in a gated community, genuinely close to Snow Canyon. Upscale golf resort and pricier than the others — included because it is the property actually near the park

items.title: A last morning on the Pa'rus Trail
items.detail: A slow paved mile along the river before you leave the canyon. Skipping it simply gets you to Kolob an hour earlier.

items.title: Check out of Springdale
items.detail: Load up. Today is the shortest driving day of the trip that still moves you somewhere.

items.title: Drive to Kolob Canyons
items.detail: UT-9 west then I-15 north. Kolob has its own entrance off the interstate at exit 40 — it is not connected to Zion Canyon by road.

items.title: Kolob Canyons — Zion's other half
items.detail: A five-mile scenic drive into blood-red finger canyons that most Zion visitors never see. Your Zion pass already covers it. Almost no crowds, and the payoff-per-minute is the best in the park.

items.title: Picnic lunch at the Kolob Canyons Viewpoint
items.detail: There are tables at the end of the drive looking straight into the canyons. Buy lunch in Springdale before you leave — there is no food at Kolob at all.

items.title: Drive to Snow Canyon
items.detail: I-15 south past St. George, then up and over into the Red Cliffs. A pretty, easy 45 minutes.

items.title: Snow Canyon State Park
items.detail: Petrified sand dunes the kids can scramble on, black lava tubes, and Jenny's Canyon — a 0.5-mile round trip into a slot barely wider than your shoulders. Warmer than Zion by ten degrees and far less busy.

items.title: Drive to Black Desert Resort, Ivins
items.detail: Ten minutes down the road. You are practically next door.

items.title: Check in at Black Desert Resort
items.detail: The nice one, on the travel credit. Two nights. Pools, lawns, and black lava rock everywhere.

items.title: Dinner at the resort
items.detail: On site, so nobody gets back in the car. Sunset is 6:50.

tips: Snow Canyon opens at 6 AM; entry $10/vehicle (state park — NPS passes not accepted).

momNotes.text: Circled "70–76°F" — she's noting St. George as the warm stretch of the trip.
Question mark next to Inn on the Cliff.

days.title: Ivins — Church, Friends, and a Slow Sunday

items.title: Drive to Redemption Lutheran Church
items.detail: St. George is about fifteen minutes from Ivins.

items.title: Worship at Redemption Lutheran Church
items.detail: An old friend is the pastor here. Get there a few minutes early to say hello before the service rather than after.

items.title: Lunch with the Raasch family
items.detail: The reason today exists. Give it the whole middle of the day and do not schedule against it.

items.title: Drive back to the resort
items.detail: Fifteen minutes.

items.title: Back to the resort — the actual rest of the trip
items.detail: This is the one genuinely unstructured block on the calendar. Pool, nap, laundry, nothing. Day eight through twelve are relentless, and this afternoon is what makes them survivable.

items.title: Pioneer Park, St. George
items.detail: Only if anyone still has energy — the point of today is that nobody has to. Red sandstone boulders, slots and arches to scramble through, fifteen minutes away and free.

items.title: Dinner — last warm night of the trip
items.detail: About 70°F today. From tomorrow you are at 8,000 ft and it will not be warm again.

tips: Confirm the service time on redemptionsg.com closer to the date — small churches move things.
Reach out about lunch weeks ahead, not the week of.
Snow Canyon is ten minutes away if anyone wants a walk, but Sunday is meant to be unhurried — only go if everyone is up early and keen.
Dinosaur Discovery Site at Johnson Farm is the fallback if the afternoon wants filling — book at utahdinosaurs.com, typically 10 AM–6 PM.

momNotes.text: Wrote "could skip & rest" against the Sunday afternoon. That is now the plan: church, lunch with friends, and nothing compulsory after it.
Underlined "tonight is the last warm night of the trip."

days.title: Ivins → Red Canyon → Bryce Canyon

options.name: Bryce Canyon Lodge
options.note: Rustic historic lodge inside the park, incomparable location. Main Lodge and Suites run Mar 1 – Nov 30 2026, so your dates are in season — but it is the only lodging inside the park and books up to a year out

options.name: Ruby's Inn (Best Western)
options.note: Full-service resort just outside the park gate, pools, restaurant, very family-friendly

options.name: Bryce Canyon Resort
options.note: Comfortable motel-style, good value, 3 miles from park gate

items.title: Check out of Black Desert
items.detail: Pack the warm layers where you can reach them — you gain 6,000 feet today.

items.title: Drive to Cedar Breaks
items.detail: I-15 north to Cedar City, then UT-14 climbs hard to 10,000 ft. Skipping Cedar Breaks makes this a straight 1 hr 50 min run to Panguitch instead.

items.title: Cedar Breaks National Monument
items.detail: A half-mile-deep amphitheatre of orange and white rock at 10,350 ft — like Bryce but emptier and a thousand feet higher. It is genuinely cold up here in late October and the rim road can close on early snow. Check before you commit to the climb.

items.title: Drive to Panguitch
items.detail: Down off the plateau on UT-143 and UT-89. Steep grades and cattle on the road.

items.title: Lunch in Panguitch
items.detail: A 19th-century brick main street and the last real town before Bryce. Also the last reasonably priced petrol.

items.title: Drive to Red Canyon
items.detail: UT-12 east. The highway runs through two arches cut in the red rock — you drive straight through them.

items.title: Red Canyon (Dixie NF)
items.detail: Bryce-orange hoodoos right beside the highway, with a visitor center and a flat paved path. Free, uncrowded, and a genuinely good warm-up for tomorrow.

items.title: Drive to Mossy Cave
items.detail: UT-12 east then a short run down UT-63.

items.title: Mossy Cave Trail
items.detail: A 0.8-mile round trip to a small waterfall and a dripping mossy grotto — inside Bryce Canyon but outside the main amphitheatre, with its own trailhead and no shuttle. Easy grade, and the waterfall is the bit the three-year-old will remember.

items.title: Drive to Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Back up UT-12 and south on UT-63 to the park gate.

items.title: Check in at Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Get the warm clothes out now. It will be near freezing at sunrise tomorrow.

items.title: Dinner in Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Early, so that sunset does not collide with a hungry three-year-old. Options are limited up here — the lodge and a handful of places by the park gate.

items.title: Sunset Point for the sunset
items.detail: Sunset is 6:44. Sunset Point is five minutes inside the gate and the hoodoos light up from the side. Bring every layer you own — it drops below freezing fast once the sun is off the rim.

tips: Bryce rim sits at 8,000–9,100 ft — coming from St. George at 2,800 ft is a big jump.
Drink lots of water; short walks only on arrival day. Altitude can cause headaches in seniors.
Temps drop sharply: overnight lows around 28–32°F. Have warm layers ready.

momNotes.text: Circled the "28–32°F" overnight lows — she wants everyone to have real cold-weather layers for Bryce.

days.title: Bryce Canyon — Full Day

items.title: Drive to Sunrise Point
items.detail: Ten minutes from town, inside the park. Go in the car — it is far too cold to wait for a shuttle.

items.title: Sunrise at Sunrise Point
items.detail: Sunrise is 7:42. The hoodoos catch the light from the bottom up and glow from the inside. It will be around 25°F — hats, gloves, blankets, and a thermos. Twenty minutes of this is worth the alarm.

items.title: Breakfast back at the lodge
items.detail: Everyone will be frozen. A hot breakfast indoors before anything else happens.

items.title: Queen's Garden Trail (1.8 mi RT, moderate)
items.detail: The gentlest way down among the hoodoos — 320 feet of descent on switchbacks, then the same back up. Do it in the morning while it is cool and everyone is fresh. Carry the three-year-old for the climb out and budget the full two hours.

items.title: Rim Trail: Sunrise to Sunset Point (1.8 mi, easy)
items.detail: Flat, paved and along the rim between the two viewpoints, with the whole amphitheatre on your left the entire way. Walk it one way and ride the shuttle back if legs are done.

items.title: Lunch at the Bryce Canyon Lodge
items.detail: Inside the park, five minutes from the rim, so you do not lose the afternoon driving out and back.

items.title: Drive south to Rainbow Point
items.detail: The park road climbs to 9,115 ft at the far end. Do the drive out in one go and stop at the overlooks on the way back — they are all on the right-hand side heading north.

items.title: Rainbow Point and the overlooks northbound
items.detail: Rainbow Point, Yovimpa Point, then Agua Canyon, Natural Bridge and Farview on the way back. A different park from the amphitheatre — high forest, long views into Arizona. Mostly done from the car, which by day nine is a feature.

items.title: Drive back to Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Back up the park road and out the gate.

items.title: Dinner in Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: Early again. Tomorrow is Scenic Byway 12, which deserves a rested crew.

tips: Rim Trail and all main viewpoints are accessible for moderate-fitness seniors.
Inspiration Point gives the widest panorama of the main amphitheater — don't miss it.
Park entry by America the Beautiful / Senior Pass.
Weather changes fast — always bring a warm layer even on sunny afternoon hikes.

momNotes.text: Underlined "Weather changes fast" and "below freezing." Cold is her main concern for the Bryce nights.
Circled "Senior Pass" once more.

days.title: Bryce → Scenic Byway 12 → Capitol Reef

options.name: Capitol Reef Resort
options.note: Lovely property in Torrey with Western-themed cabins and great views; very limited rooms

options.name: Austin's Chuckwagon Motel
options.note: Classic Western motel, local institution, Torrey town center

items.title: Depart Bryce Canyon City
items.detail: A later start than the other driving days — today is the road itself, and leaving at 9:15 puts you in Boulder exactly at lunchtime.

items.title: Drive to Kodachrome Basin
items.detail: UT-12 east then a short spur south from Cannonville.

items.title: Kodachrome Basin State Park
items.detail: Sixty-seven sandstone chimneys standing straight up out of the desert floor — sedimentary pipes left behind when the softer rock eroded away. Named by a National Geographic expedition in 1948. The Grand Parade trail is flat and short.

items.title: Drive Scenic Byway 12 to Boulder
items.detail: The heart of the trip's best road: over Escalante, then the Hogback — a mile-long stretch of two-lane with a thousand-foot drop off both sides at once and no shoulder. Slow down, use the pullouts. Without the Kodachrome stop this leg runs 76 mi / 1 hr 30 min direct from Bryce.

items.title: Lunch in Boulder
items.detail: A town of 250 people with a genuinely good place to eat. It was supplied by pack mule until 1940 — the last place in the lower 48 to get its mail that way.

items.title: Anasazi State Park Museum, Boulder
items.detail: An excavated Ancestral Puebloan village of about 87 rooms, occupied around AD 1160, with a full-size six-room replica dwelling you can walk into. Small, indoors, air-conditioned and quick — a good reset between two long drives.

items.title: Drive to Capitol Reef
items.detail: UT-12 climbs over Boulder Mountain to 9,600 ft with long views back across the Escalante, then drops to Torrey and east into the park.

items.title: Capitol Reef — Fruita district
items.detail: A green orchard valley in the middle of red rock: a Mormon pioneer settlement with fruit trees you may pick from, a one-room schoolhouse, and deer everywhere at dusk. The most relaxed national park on the route by a distance.

items.title: Gifford Homestead — the pie
items.detail: A restored 1908 farmhouse selling small fruit pies baked that morning, plus cinnamon rolls and ice cream. It closes at 5:00 PM and regularly sells out well before then, so treat 3:30 as a real deadline rather than a suggestion.

items.title: Hickman Bridge Trail (1 mi RT)
items.detail: A natural bridge 133 feet across, reached by a 400-foot climb over slickrock. Genuinely steep in the first quarter mile — an hour and a half with small children, and it puts dinner back to 6:00.

items.title: Drive to Torrey
items.detail: Twelve miles west, back out of the park.

items.title: Dinner in Torrey
items.detail: A small town with a few genuinely good restaurants. Sunset is 6:38. Early night — tomorrow starts at 7:30.

tips: The lightest driving day of the trip, which is why it can absorb Kodachrome Basin (about 35 minutes round trip) without strain.
Gifford Homestead closes in the late afternoon and sells out of pie before that. Go there before Hickman Bridge.
Fill the tank in Escalante or Boulder; services on Byway 12 are thin.

momNotes.text: Wrote "Mmm" next to the Gifford Homestead pies — the apple pie is non-negotiable.
Checked Capitol Reef Resort and Austin's Chuckwagon Motel. Torrey Schoolhouse B&B and Skyridge Inn are real alternatives if you want a third choice.

days.title: Capitol Reef → Goblin Valley → Arches

options.name: SpringHill Suites Moab
options.note: Booked with the Marriott free-night certificate. All-suite, free breakfast, pool, and a separate living area — useful when the toddler goes down before the adults do. Arriving late after the longest driving day of the trip, so a suite and a breakfast you don't have to go find are worth more here than the view would be

options.name: Hyatt Place Moab
options.note: Modern, pool, river views, very comfortable for family groups

options.name: Hoodoo Moab, Curio by Hilton
options.note: Stylish, central, walkable to restaurants

options.name: Moab Valley Inn
options.note: Reliable, spacious rooms, easy parking, good value

options.name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Moab
options.note: The neighbouring Marriott and the designated overflow if SpringHill is unavailable — also the closest hotel in town to the Arches entrance

items.title: Depart Torrey — UT-24 east
items.detail: An early start buys you the whole afternoon in Arches, which is the point of today.

items.title: Drive to Goblin Valley
items.detail: UT-24 east across the San Rafael Swell — empty, strange country the whole way.

items.title: Goblin Valley State Park
items.detail: A valley floor covered in thousands of squat mushroom-shaped hoodoos, and the rarest thing in any park: you are allowed to leave the trail and let children loose to climb on them. This is the best ninety minutes of the trip for a three-year-old.

items.title: Little Wild Horse Canyon
items.detail: A genuine slot canyon fifteen minutes from Goblin Valley, narrow enough to touch both walls. The full loop is eight miles, but the good part starts immediately and an hour in and out is worthwhile. Realistically it costs 2 hr 30 min with the drive — which comes straight out of the Arches afternoon. Never enter if there is any chance of rain.

items.title: Drive to Green River
items.detail: North out of Goblin Valley to I-70.

items.title: Lunch in Green River
items.detail: A highway town on the river, and the only real food between Goblin Valley and Moab. Fuel up here.

items.title: Canyonlands NP — Island in the Sky
items.detail: Mesa Arch framing the canyon, and Grand View Point looking two thousand feet down into the Green River gorge. Genuinely world-class — and it is an hour and a quarter out from Green River plus two hours there plus an hour back to Arches. That is the whole Arches afternoon. This is the fork in the road: take Canyonlands instead of Arches, not as well as it.

items.title: Dead Horse Point State Park
items.detail: A 2,000-foot overlook onto a gooseneck of the Colorado, on the same spur road out to Canyonlands. Only worth it if you have already chosen that road — on its own it is a 1 hr 40 min detour for a single view.

items.title: Drive to Arches — Park Avenue
items.detail: I-70 east then US-191 south. The park entrance is five miles north of Moab and Park Avenue is the first stop inside it.

items.title: Arches — Park Avenue and Courthouse Towers
items.detail: Start at the bottom of the park and work up. Park Avenue is a canyon of vertical sandstone slabs standing in rows like buildings; the overlook takes five minutes and the trail down into it is a flat mile if you want it.

items.title: Drive up to Balanced Rock
items.detail: The park road climbs past the Petrified Dunes with the La Sal Mountains behind them.

items.title: Balanced Rock and the Windows section
items.detail: A 3,600-ton boulder on a slender pedestal, then the Windows: North and South Window and Turret Arch, all reached by short flat gravel paths from one car park. The highest density of arches in the park and the easiest walking — this is the heart of the visit.

items.title: Drive to the Delicate Arch viewpoint
items.detail: Ten minutes north, then a short spur east.

items.title: Delicate Arch viewpoint
items.detail: The famous one. The hike to stand under it is 3 miles round trip up open slickrock with no shade and a sheer drop at the end — not with a three-year-old and a newborn. The lower viewpoint is a flat 100 yards from the car park and shows you the arch across the canyon.

items.title: Drive back to Balanced Rock
items.detail: Ten minutes back down the park road.

items.title: Picnic dinner at the Balanced Rock picnic area
items.detail: There are tables here with the rock right above you. Eating in the park rather than driving back to Moab is what buys you the golden hour — pick the food up in Green River at lunch and carry it. No water at these tables, so bring your own.

items.title: Golden hour at the Windows
items.detail: Sunset is 6:30. The last half hour of light on the Windows is the best light in the park, and by then almost everyone else has driven out to dinner. Five minutes back down the road from the picnic area.

items.title: Drive to SpringHill Suites Moab
items.detail: Out the park road and south into town.

items.title: Arrive SpringHill Suites Moab
items.detail: Last night on the road. Pack tonight — tomorrow is the long drive home.

tips: Arches gets the whole afternoon on purpose — 1:00 PM to 6:45 PM, finishing at golden hour in the Windows.
Canyonlands is the fork: it costs the Arches afternoon almost exactly. Pick one. Dead Horse Point sits on the same spur road.
Carry dinner out of Green River. Eating at the Balanced Rock picnic tables is what buys you the last light instead of driving to Moab for it.
Goblin Valley entry ~$25/vehicle — a state park, not covered by the Senior Pass or the park pass.
Closed-toe shoes for Goblin Valley; the sandstone shreds bare feet.
No timed entry permit required for Arches in late October.

momNotes.text: Circled "Pack a full lunch" — even more true now that Goblin Valley is on this leg. Nothing between Torrey and Green River.
Circled "Senior Pass" for the Arches entry. Note it does not cover Goblin Valley or Dead Horse Point.

days.title: Moab → Glenwood Canyon → Fort Collins

items.title: Depart Moab
items.detail: Breakfast at the hotel, on the road by 8:00. Six and a half hours of driving today plus stops.

items.title: Leave Moab on UT-128 instead of US-191
items.detail: The river road: fifty miles along the Colorado under red cliffs, rejoining I-70 near Cisco. Adds about 45 minutes to a day that is already long, and it is the prettiest road on the trip.

items.title: Drive to Glenwood Springs
items.detail: US-191 north to I-70, then east through Grand Junction and up Glenwood Canyon — the canyon stretch is genuinely spectacular from the interstate.

items.title: Lunch in Glenwood Springs
items.detail: Downtown, five minutes from the caverns tram. Sit down properly — there is a lot of car left.

items.title: Glenwood Caverns Adventure Park
items.detail: A gondola up the canyon wall to cave tours, a viewing platform over the town and an alpine coaster. The cave tour is the part worth booking. The one stop of the day, so it gets the whole afternoon — buy tram tickets ahead, October hours are reduced.

items.title: Drive to Silverthorne
items.detail: I-70 east over Vail Pass. Weather can turn on this stretch in late October — check CDOT before you leave Glenwood.

items.title: Dinner in Silverthorne
items.detail: Two hours from home, which is exactly the right place to stop. Feeding everyone here means the last leg is quiet and dark and nobody is desperate.

items.title: Drive home to Fort Collins
items.detail: I-70 east through the Eisenhower Tunnel, then north. Mostly downhill and mostly asleep.

items.title: Home in Fort Collins
items.detail: Twelve days, five national parks, five state parks, and about 2,100 miles.

tips: Leave Moab no later than 8 AM to reach Glenwood with time for activities.
Glenwood Caverns is the one stop today. It gets the whole afternoon, which is why the day still lands home by 8 PM.
Glenwood Canyon on I-70 is itself spectacular; stop at the Hanging Lake trailhead pullout just to see the canyon walls.
Check CDOT.com for Eisenhower Tunnel / I-70 mountain corridor conditions before departure.

momNotes.text: Wrote "1st choice" next to Glenwood Caverns / King's Row Cave tour — that settles the Caverns-vs-Hot-Springs question in favor of the Caverns.

bookings.notes: Ouray is a town of 1,000 and October rooms are limited — book early. Prefer a lodge with its own hot-spring tubs (Box Canyon, Twin Peaks); it gives you the soak without spending a time slot on it.
No reservation — pay at the gate, about $30 for the group. Ring 970-325-7080 to confirm October hours; the park runs 9:00–5:00 from Oct 15 and slightly longer before that.
Ten minutes from the Mesa Verde gate, which is what buys you the early start on Day 3. Chains only; book early for the indoor pool.

bookings.what: Goulding's Lodge, Monument Valley — night of Oct 14
bookings.notes: The only full-service lodging at Monument Valley — there is nothing else within an hour, so book promptly. Ask for a valley-facing room; the terrace is where you watch sunset.

bookings.what: Cable Mountain Lodge, Springdale — nights of Oct 15 & 16
bookings.notes: Mom's 1st choice. Desert Pearl Inn is her 2nd.

bookings.what: Black Desert Resort, Ivins — nights of Oct 17 & 18
bookings.notes: The Chase-credit stay, and the one restful stretch of the trip. Book PREPAID ("Pay Now") for both nights in a single transaction through Chase Travel — The Edit needs 2+ nights and pays a maximum of $250 per transaction, so a 2-night stay captures $250, not $500. The card has to pay but the parents can be the named guests. Black Desert is independent, so the separate $250 select-hotels credit (IHG, Minor, Montage, Omni, Pan Pacific, Pendry, Virgin) does NOT apply here. Confirm the resort actually appears in The Edit before relying on it — the public lists I checked showed no Utah properties, though inventory changes. The annual travel credit renews 9/5/2026 and has no brand or night restriction, so it can cover the balance.

bookings.what: Capitol Reef Resort, Torrey — night of Oct 21
bookings.notes: Very limited rooms in a tiny town. Mom checked this one and Austin's Chuckwagon.

bookings.what: Bryce Canyon lodging — nights of Oct 19 & 20
bookings.notes: The Lodge at Bryce Canyon's Main Lodge and Suites run Mar 1 – Nov 30, 2026, so your dates are in season. It is the only lodging inside the park and books up to a year out — visitbrycecanyon.com.

bookings.what: SpringHill Suites Moab — night of Oct 22
bookings.notes: Redeeming the Marriott free-night certificate. Two things to check before counting on it: the certificate's points cap (35k Boundless/Bold, 50k Brilliant, 85k on some — you may top off by up to 15,000 points) against a peak-season Thursday in Moab, and that the certificate is still valid through October 2026. Award inventory in a small market during Arches season goes early, so book as soon as the certificate allows. One further check: SpringHill has run an autumn renovation closure in a recent year (Nov 14 – Dec 26), which misses these dates, but reconfirm when booking since those schedules move. Fairfield Inn next door is the fallback and takes the same certificate.

bookings.what: Mesa Verde Cliff Palace ranger tour (Oct 14)
bookings.notes: $5/person, recreation.gov. Reduced October schedule and it fills fast. Book a mid-morning slot — you are on site 8:35–11:35 on the drive out to Monument Valley.

bookings.what: Glenwood Caverns — King's Row Cave tour (Oct 23)
bookings.notes: Mom's 1st choice for the final day.

bookings.what: America the Beautiful pass ($80/yr) or Senior Pass
bookings.notes: Mom has a Senior Pass (free lifetime, 62+) — circled it on five separate pages. Covers Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, Bryce, Zion, Mesa Verde entry. Does NOT cover Monument Valley ($20/vehicle), Snow Canyon ($10/vehicle), Goblin Valley (~$25/vehicle), or Dead Horse Point.
October mountain weather can delay plans.

bookings.what: Arrange Sunday lunch with the Raasch family (Oct 18)
bookings.notes: Worship 10:00 AM at Redemption Lutheran, 348 N Bluff St. Reach out well ahead — Sunday mornings are working time for a pastor.

bookings.what: Confirm a vehicle that seats six with two car seats
bookings.notes: Four adults, a toddler car seat, an infant seat and twelve days of luggage. A standard five-seat SUV does not do this. If the family car won't take it, a rental needs booking well ahead — October is still busy in Denver.

bookings.what: Utah state park entry fees — pay at each gate
bookings.notes: Snow Canyon $10, Goblin Valley ~$25, Dead Horse Point ~$20, plus Goosenecks ~$5 and Kodachrome ~$10 if you take those options. Roughly $55–70 total. A non-resident annual pass runs about $175, so it is NOT worth buying for this route. None of these are covered by the America the Beautiful pass.

bookings.what: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary tour, Kanab (Oct 15)
bookings.notes: Free, but the 90-minute bus tours must be reserved ahead and do fill. Only if Day 4 is the day you pick it — see the three optional stops on that day, of which you should do one.

items: America the Beautiful annual pass, or Mom's Senior Pass — covers entry to Zion, Bryce, Capitol Reef, Arches, Canyonlands and Mesa Verde. The Senior Pass holder has to be in the vehicle and show it.
Cash and a card. Monument Valley Navajo Tribal Park is $20/vehicle and the Utah state park gates vary — a few are cash-only, a few are card-only.
Printed confirmations for the D&SNG train and any timed tours. Cell signal at the depot and in the parks is unreliable.
Layers, seriously. Mornings at Bryce are near 25°F; afternoons in the St. George area are near 75°F.
Warm hat, gloves and a real coat for every adult. Bryce Point after dark is below freezing and you will be standing still for half an hour.
Child's warm hat, mittens and puffy coat for the two Bryce days.
Sun hats and sunglasses for everyone, including the kids.
Church clothes for Sunday morning at Redemption Lutheran on Oct 18.
Swimsuits — several of the hotels have pools, and the Ouray lodges have their own hot-spring soaking tubs.
More toddler clothes than seems reasonable, plus a complete change kept in the car.
Waterproof hiking shoes for the whole family. October trails can be icy in the morning and wet after rain.
Closed-toe shoes for Goblin Valley and Little Wild Horse Canyon — the sandstone destroys sandals and bare feet.
A bag or ziplocs for sandy shoes before they go back in the car.
Trekking poles for the grandparents if they use them; Queen's Garden drops 320 ft on loose rock.
Infant carrier or wrap. Most of the best viewpoints are short walks on uneven ground, not stroller terrain.
Far more diapers and wipes than the trip length suggests. Torrey, Bluff and Monument Valley have almost nowhere to restock.
Portable changing mat — many trailhead restrooms have no table.
Feeding supplies and a way to warm a bottle in the car.
Sun shade for the car window and for the carrier. Sunscreen isn't recommended under six months, so shade and long sleeves do the work.
Confirm a crib with each hotel rather than assuming, or bring a travel one.
Saline drops. The air is extremely dry and Bryce sits at 8,000 ft.
Carrier for when she runs out of steam, which will happen at the furthest point from the car.
Stroller for the paved stretches: Pa'rus Trail, the Bryce Rim Trail, the Dead Horse Point rim loop.
Sand toys for Goblin Valley.
Downloaded shows and audiobooks. There is no signal for most of the driving.
Reusable bottles, a liter per person per hike, plus a couple of gallon jugs in the trunk.
A cooler. Day 1 and Day 11 both have long stretches with nothing open.
Far more snacks than you think. Mom circled "pack a full lunch" for a reason (M18).
Download offline maps for the whole route before leaving. There is no signal on Byway 12, around Goblin Valley, or through much of the Navajo Nation.
Phone mounts, car chargers and a power bank.
Check the spare tire and pressures before departure. Monument Valley's Valley Drive and Valley of the Gods are washboard dirt.
Motion sickness remedy — Wolf Creek Pass, Byway 12 and the road down to Bryce are all winding.
Trash bags. Several of these stops have no bins.
Sunscreen. The October desert sun is still strong, more so at 8,000 ft.
SPF lip balm and a heavy moisturizer. The dryness catches everyone out by about day three.
First aid kit with blister bandages, ibuprofen and antihistamines.
Any prescriptions, with a few days spare in case weather delays you.
Altitude is a real factor for the grandparents: Wolf Creek Pass is 10,857 ft on Day 1 and Bryce is 8,000–9,100 ft for two nights. Drink more water than feels necessary.
Headlamps, ideally with a red-light mode so nobody wrecks everyone's night vision at Bryce Point.
A blanket each for stargazing. You'll be stationary in sub-freezing air.
Binoculars — good for the Milky Way at night and the viewpoints by day.
A star chart or app downloaded in advance; there's no signal at Bryce Point.
The good camera for the Monument Valley sunset and the Bryce sunrise, plus spare batteries — cold drains them fast.
